evidence: Each count is traceable to a read date and a coverage decision, not to a disagreement about a score.

impact: Blocks R-29, R-41, R-50 and the replacement-depth half of R-06.

finding: Only the current season's weekly reports are exposed by the page, so designation reliability and any multi-season rule cannot be measured.
evidence: Week selector exposes 2026 weeks 1-10 plus prior seasons' weeks only where the league renders them.
impact: Keeps R-63 and R-50 open; keeps the train/validation/holdout split within one season.
proposed_action: Seek a licensed archive; otherwise keep the within-season chronology and say so.

finding: The league's dated schedule-announcement document was not located in this session's reads, so R-24 stays open instead of being satisfied by the live schedule page.
evidence: The by-week page carries the flexible-scheduling text but not a dated announcement.
impact: The 'published schedule facts' feature set lacks the announcement that authorises its own dates.
proposed_action: Ask for the canonical announcement URL; do not substitute a news article for it.

finding: No transactions log was read this session, so roster turnover is not yet a versioned data event.
evidence: The requirement (R-31) explicitly wants depth/availability versioned against the last official roster event.
impact: Stale rows (e.g. a traded or IR'd player still printed in a depth view) cannot be detected here.
proposed_action: Add a dated transactions capture to the same weekly job as the report.

finding: The standings table renders split-record columns that its own LEGEND does not define.
evidence: LEGEND defines W, L, T, PCT, HOME, ROAD, DIV, CONF, PF, PA, NET PTS, STRK; the rendered row has more numeric groups than that.
impact: Only LEGEND-defined columns are used by this pack; the others are not published at all.
proposed_action: Either restrict the site to defined columns or publish the LEGEND gap beside the table (done here).

finding: Record badges on a by-week page are as-of-render, and clubs with a game in progress show their pre-game record.
evidence: At read time three Week 10 games were live; those six clubs show records that exclude the in-progress game, while clubs whose games had finished show updated records.
impact: Any 'through week N' aggregate built from a badge during a live week is wrong for exactly those clubs.
proposed_action: Reconcile against a finals-only corpus (done here: 220 identities) and never read a badge as a week-ending record.

finding: The official report uses no percentages for 'Questionable'; any play-rate number attached to a designation is folklore.
evidence: Column headers are Player, Position, Injuries, Practice Status, Game Status.
